summary: The compiler ran five full, irrelevant NodeTransformer traversals for straight-line functions. A single conservative source-node inventory now skips passes that cannot apply, while dependency triggers retain downstream passes for nodes generated by earlier rewrites. On a 1,000-statement function, fresh-process median rewrite time fell from 58.199 ms to 25.640 ms (56.0%) and transformer visits fell from 40,031 to 1.

remaining_limitations: The optimization targets Python AST traversal and changes no C++ native code, so the prepared native rebuild was not applicable. Timing is intentionally a synthetic large straight-line function to isolate AST rewrite overhead; end-to-end compilation speedup depends on function syntax and later compiler costs.
